content.text: {"tools":[{"name":"Flat","url":null},{"name":"IVF","url":null},{"name":"HNSW","url":null},{"name":"IVF-PQ","url":null},{"name":"ScaNN","url":null}],"on_screen_text":"","key_claims":["Flat checks every stored vector and looks for exact closest matches, but more documents means more work","IVF groups similar vectors and searches a few nearby groups, resulting in fewer comparisons but it can miss matches elsewhere","HNSW follows connections through layers of vectors that shortcut like a map, making search fast but requiring extra memory for connections","IVF compares full vectors inside groups, while IVF-PQ splits vectors into parts and stores small codes for them, saving memory and making comparison cheaper but less precise","ScaNN is Google's system that combines grouping and compressed comparisons to make a shortlist, then checks that shortlist more accurately so detailed comparisons happen on fewer candidates","The trade-offs among these methods are speed, memory usage, and recall (how many of the closest matches you find)"],"info_channel":"spoken"}
